stem.text: Consider the curve \( y^{2} = x^{2}(x + 27) \). There are exactly two points on this curve at which the tangent line is horizontal. Find the \( y \)-coordinate of the one at which \( \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} > 0 \).

worked_solution.text: Differentiate implicitly: \( 2y\frac{dy}{dx} = 3 x^{2} + 54 x \), so \( \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3 x^{2} + 54 x}{2y} \). The numerator is 0 at \( x = 0 \) and at \( x = -18 \). At \( x = 0 \) the curve gives \( y = 0 \), where the denominator is also 0, so there is no horizontal tangent there. At \( x = -18 \), \( y^{2} = 2916 \), so \( y = \pm 54 \) and the denominator is not 0.
Differentiate again, keeping \( y \) as a function of \( x \): \( 2\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^{2} + 2y\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 6 x + 54 \).
At both points \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 0 \) and \( x = -18 \), so \( \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{-54}{2y} \). At \( y = -54 \) this is \( \frac{1}{2} \), and at \( y = 54 \) it is \( - \frac{1}{2} \).
The second derivative is positive at \( (-18, -54) \), so the \( y \)-coordinate is \( -54 \).

parameter_draw.task: horizontal tangent point selected by the sign of the second derivative
